utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning, the technical booth, the interpreters, the legal officers, the court reporters; good morning to the Prosecution; good morning to the Defence; good morning to General Krstic; good morning, Witness. We have a witness in the courtroom already. Before beginning I should like to inform you that Judge Fouad Riad is unable to be with us today and we are therefore going to sit in accordance with Article 15 bis, because there are urgent reasons of ill-health that are keeping him away and we are going to continue the hearings. Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're going to read the solemn declaration which the usher is going to hand to you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated, madam. Are you feeling comfortable? You are now going to answer questions put to you by Mr. Cayley, whom you see to your right. Mr. Cayley, the witness is yours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Judge Wald, my learned friends for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to call you "Witness T" during your evidence in order to protect your identity. But first of all could you please look at the name written on the piece of paper. Don't read it out, just confirm that that is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, please relax as best you can. I know it's not easy speaking about these events, and I only have a few questions for you, as you know. Just a few preliminary questions. You're of Bosnian nationality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You are a Muslim by faith.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I didn't -- oh, there is a response on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In July of 1995 I think you were living in a village that was inside the Srebrenica enclave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: After the enclave fell in July of 1995, I think you went to the woods with your children and with other women from the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I know you spent a number of nights in the woods and I'm not going to ask you about that, but I think I'm right in saying that you arrived in Potocari on the 11th of July of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When you arrived in Potocari, can you tell the Judges where you went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I was in front of a factory. We got there and we spent the night there. On the 11th, in the evening, UNPROFOR was around us and whoever entered, they said they couldn't get out again, so it was safer to stay there, they said. During the night and the next night in the evening, the 12th in the evening, the Serbs came and in the evening they took people away and killed them, slaughtered, and did all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you can just wait there for one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/7. Mr. Usher, I have a copy. You can borrow mine. If you could put it in front of the witness and then put it on the ELMO. THE USHER: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the building in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what this building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Is this the building where you stayed outside when you arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could it be placed on the ELMO, please. Would you move it down, please, and if the lens could be withdrawn so that we can see the whole photograph. That's fine. Let the record show that the witness has identified Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/7 as the factory building where she and her children remained outside after she arrived in Potocari. Mr. Usher, that's fine. You can leave that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I want you to cast your mind back to the night of the 12th of July when you and your children were outside this factory building. I think there was a woman nearby to you with three sons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Judges what you saw take place on that night.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: First, two elderly -- there were two older boys, they were resisting, and then in the end they took all three of them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you say that there were two older boys, they were resisting, and in the end they took all three away. Who took the three boys away; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How were these Serbs dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They had on military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you want to take a break at any time, just indicate to the President, if you want to just take a five-minute break, and I'm sure we can do that. Do you want to continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How old were these three boys, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I think the oldest was between 18 and 20. The next one, between 10 and 15. Judging by their height, that is my judgement. And the young one was between five and seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where did these Serbs in military uniform take these three boys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Behind the factory, around that second corner there [indicates], and he killed them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you see them being killed behind the factory building that's on the screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I didn't see them being killed, but I saw them later. I saw them dead. I didn't see them when they were actually being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What time had passed between the Serb soldiers taking them away and you seeing them behind the building; how much time passed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: About an hour, I think. She fainted, and she was looking for her sons. We went round to see them, and then she fainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who fainted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Their mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you describe -- I know this is very difficult, and we'll move through it as quickly as we can. Can you describe to the Judges, when you saw the three bodies behind the factory, what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: All three were one next to another. They were covered up to their waists, and all three had their throats slit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: After you had seen these three bodies, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: What did I do? Nothing. First, when they took those three children, she fainted. When she came to, she wanted to know where they were. She first asked about the youngest one. Then we told her that they had taken all three. We went to look. Then she fainted again. We dragged her back to where she was before, and that's how it was. When again she came to, we gave her some pills to take, and that's how it was. Later, they came again. They took another two, but they were older people. I don't know exactly how old they were. They weren't too old or too young, maybe about 30 or 35. They took them too, and they slaughtered the two of them too right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just wait a moment. You said they came again and took two others. Were these two others another two Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And who took them away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: The same two. After having killed the three children, the same two came to take them away. They took two away, and one of them never returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And "the same two," you're referring to the two Serb soldiers who had originally come to take the children away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. They came back for these two older men, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: After those older men had been taken away, did you see them again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: They were only on the other side. They were also killed, and both of them had also had their throats slit in the same way as the three children, only they were turned around in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you see those two other bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Again, behind this factory where these three were, these three children, and then next to them were these two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you recall when you saw those other two bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it was about two hours later, after we had seen these three, because we had to carry the woman back. They took these other two while the woman was unconscious. When the woman came to, then there were two other women whom I saw for the first time, and they went to see, and they saw the same thing and a lot of blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I think on the 13th of July, I'm correct in saying that you and your children left Potocari by bus, and you were taken eventually to the free territory in Tuzla; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. When I had seen all that, I picked up my children and headed to the buses. And about 10 past 2.00, I think -- this was the second set of buses, and we got on and headed towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for the witness, and I can now offer her for cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Cayley. Mr. Petrusic, you have the witness for cross-examination, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, my learned friends of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Good morning, madam. I shall really try to be very brief. Madam, I wouldn't like to go through the statement that you gave to the Prosecution in August 1995, but I would have a question for you, and that is: Did you see, in Potocari, the separation of men from women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that occasion when this separation was carried out, did you notice any police dogs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Madam T, after these events which you have described to Mr. Cayley, did you see members of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know. I know I saw some people; I think they were UNPROFOR. They may have been Serbs dressed in their clothing. But I did see blue uniforms on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This group that you were in and which was aware of these events, or perhaps you yourself, did you inform UNPROFOR members of what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: We did say these things but they said it wasn't true. But everything was visible during the night of the 12th. There were so many atrocities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. During this second arrival of the two soldiers, are you sure that they took away two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Madam, in your statement to the Prosecution you said you saw a couple, a husband and wife.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, those were two men. But later they separated the husband from a wife, because they had two children. UNPROFOR said that nobody else could come and they took him away, and there was some corn down there and they took them down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would, after all, like to show the witness her statement, and I would end my cross-examination with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could assist my learned friend. I think it might be an idea in the case of this witness to actually highlight, if you haven't done so already, if you could put a highlighter across the section so that she can go straight to it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, that is a good suggestion, but I think it is a method that you have already adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have already done that for the convenience of the Chamber, and of course the witness. So could the usher please give the witness her previous statement, the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Madam T, is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, perhaps we need to wait for the number of the exhibit so that we can identify it. Madam Registrar, can you give us a number for this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, it is D20, Exhibit D20.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D20, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is D20. Please continue, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Madam T, is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of that statement, it is highlighted with a marker, you said, "Later that evening the same three soldiers returned who had taken these three boys away. They took away a man and a woman."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: No, they took away two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that ends my cross-examination. Madam T, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Cayley, do you have any additional re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I don't have any further questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Cayley. Judge Wald, have you any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Just two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Madam T, your children were with you in Potocari at the time that your neighbour's children were taken away by the Serb soldiers; is that right? You had your children with you around the factory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, were your children boys or girls, and about what ages were they, your own children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: One was born in 1992, the other in 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So they were very young at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Was there any reason that you could tell why they took your neighbour's children away but they didn't approach your children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: She wasn't my neighbour. I didn't even know that woman; I saw her for the first time there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But the woman who was close by that you saw, you couldn't tell why they took her children but they left your children alone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I don't know. I had two little girls, and those were boys. Maybe that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I see. My only other question is: You told us about the sad story of seeing the boys' bodies and then later on at least one of the -- if I remember correctly, did you see the bodies of the two men that were taken out later? Is that right? Did you see their bodies too, of the men that were taken out later than the three boys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I saw them later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: My only question is: Were those the only bodies you saw that night, the three boys and the two men, or were there other bodies around in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: There were but I didn't dare look. I went to the buses in the morning and I don't know what happened afterwards. There were all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. Witness T, I have only one question. The Prosecutor has asked questions, the Defence has asked questions, and my colleague Judge Wald. Is there anything else that you would like to say and that hasn't been asked of you? You may say it now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I have nothing to say. Who was there could have seen it all. I don't know. Only when I reached Tuzla, I found my mother, and she told me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take your time, Witness T. We have every understanding for your suffering.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: My mother told me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't hear that. The interpreter apologises. We think the witness said that her father had been killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, do you wish to continue or is that all you wanted to say? We feel very much for you, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: I would like to finish there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take your time, please, Witness T. What did your mother tell you? You told us that you wanted to end there with what your mother told you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T
utterances.text: That they had killed my father at Potocari a day later. That's what my mother said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Witness, we do not wish to make you suffer any further. I think that you were very brave to come here and to tell us everything that you have told us, and therefore that ends your testimony here. We wish you a safe journey to your place of residence and that you will be able to recover, because you have children who need you. Please don't move, because of protective measures, so that we are going to have a break, a 20-minute break, after which the hearing will be resumed. So thank you very much, Witness T, for coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 10.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Judge Wald. Good morning, colleagues. Your Honours, Mr. Ruez, who has testified previously in this session, in this trial, will be testifying essentially about two areas. First, I intend to ask him a number of questions to connect exhibits that have been introduced previously by witnesses, to connect them to names and to locations. But the principal part of Mr. Ruez' testimony will be to develop for the Trial Chamber the evidence that relates to the extensive efforts by the VRS to remove bodies from primary grave sites and conceal them in secondary grave sites. So let me then, with that introduction to Your Honours -- again, good morning, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, excuse me for interrupting you. I must remind the witness that he's under oath, or there may be some doubt as to whether it is necessary to take the solemn declaration or not. But to avoid all doubt, Mr. Usher, perhaps it is simpler for Mr. Ruez to take the oath once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Due to the origin of the material that we are going to exhibit today, I will testify in the English language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Ruez. Now things are quite clear as regards the solemn declaration, and you're now going to answer questions put to you by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Even though you have testified previously in this proceeding, there are people in the gallery who don't know who you are and what you do. So could you briefly identify what you do and how long you've been employed by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: My name is Jean-Rene Ruez. I am the investigation team leader for the Srebrenica investigation. I joined the Tribunal in April 1995, and I am concerned with the Srebrenica case since 20th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me begin by showing you Prosecutor's Exhibit 28, and I'm going to ask you to identify a number of individuals in Prosecutor's Exhibit 28. Let me begin, first of all, by showing you Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/7. Now, that's been placed on the ELMO. Mr. Ruez, have you met this individual?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you identify him for the Judges, please?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: His name is Colonel Cedo Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, what was his position in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic was the commander of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me show you the next Prosecutor's exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/9. Returning briefly to the previous exhibit, Mr. Ruez, you testified that Mr. Blagojevic was a colonel in the 1st Light Infantry Brigade. Was that in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Bratunac Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's go to the next exhibit, please, the one that's on the ELMO. Have you met this individual?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: He is -- he was at the time a major. His name is Dragan Obrenovic. He was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Zvornik Brigade. He's currently the commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That was on the 11th of July he held that position?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On 11 of July, 1995, he was the deputy commander of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now can we turn to 28/11. Now, this individual, Mr. Ruez, have you met this individual?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: His name is Pavle Golic. He was a Major in July 1995. He was a member of the Intelligence Section at the Drina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's turn, Mr. Usher, to 28/18, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, have you met this individual?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: His name is Svetozar Andric. He was a Lieutenant Colonel at the time of the events in July 1995. He was the commander of the 1st Bihac Sekovici -- he was the brigade commander of the Sekovici Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Usher, for the time being I'm finished with the exhibits in Prosecutor's Exhibit 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you two new exhibits that the Prosecutor will be introducing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I can have given to the usher and if they can be placed on the ELMO Prosecutor's Exhibit 185 and 186. Now, could you place Prosecutor's Exhibit 185 on the ELMO, please, and if we could have that properly shown that would be fine. Thank you very much. Now, this, Your Honours, is a still image taken from a film that has been previously introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, who is the man in the foreground in this particular picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This man is identified as being Ljubo, probably Ljubisa, family name Borovcanin. He is the deputy commander of the special police force based in Janja in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the far right you can see an image of a man, at least half of a man's face. Is that Colonel Kingori from the Kenyan forces?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Major at the time of the events and he was present in Potocari, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you another still image that has been taken from another film that has been introduced previously, Prosecutor's Exhibit 186. Can you identify the man standing to the right of the man in the blue helmet?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The man standing on the right is, again, Ljubo Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was his position on the 11th of July, 1995, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander of the special police based in Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have two new exhibits I'd like displayed on the ELMO; one is Prosecutor's Exhibit -- I'm sorry, they are old exhibits -- Prosecutor's Exhibits 71 and 72. For reference for Your Honours, this was an individual who was identified during the testimony of Lieutenant van Duijn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me put Prosecutor's Exhibit 71, first of all, on the ELMO. Referring to the man on the left-hand side of this image, can you identify him, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The man on the left is Mendeljejev Dzuric. He is a company commander from the special police force, based in Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know who his superior was?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: His superior was Ljubo Borovcanin, who was the deputy commander of that same special police force in Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could place the next exhibit on the ELMO, please, Prosecutor's Exhibit 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that the same individual that you previously identified in Prosecutor's 71?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This is again Mendeljejev Dzuric, whose rank at the time is unknown to us at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I've concluded, Mr. Usher, with those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you, Mr. Ruez, three exhibits that have been previously entered into evidence, Prosecutor's Exhibits 170, 171, and 172.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, for point of reference to Your Honours, these three exhibits are exhibits that were introduced through Mr. Erdemovic. Mr. Erdemovic identified a location where he and his colleagues went on the 16th of July. From Vlasenica they arrived at a particular location; these are the images of that particular location. From that location they were taken to the Branjevo Military Farm. There should be three images, 170, 171, and 172. Why don't we start, Mr. Usher, with Prosecutor's Exhibit 170.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, are you familiar with this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photograph which I took on the 7th of June, 1996. The buildings which can be seen on this photograph are the headquarters and the barracks of the 1st Zvornik Brigade, based in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was the Zvornik Brigade located at those structures on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, they were located at this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, could you turn to the next exhibit, Prosecutor's Exhibit 171, and place that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that an image of the same location but from a different perspective, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is the entrance gate of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Just at the right of this picture is the guardhouse of the compound where the Lieutenant Colonel who met Drazen Erdemovic's team before going to the Branjevo Farm, he met the team. He was coming out from this guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's turn to the last image, Prosecutor's Exhibit 172, and ask you just briefly to identify that as well.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is another view of the compound of the 1st Zvornik Brigade, the headquarters of the 1st Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I've finished with those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me now show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 160, and I'm going to ask you about the 5th Engineering Unit. You should have a copy, Mr. Ruez, of Prosecutor's Exhibit 160, and we're going to be referring to eight exhibits, 160/1 through 160/8. First of all, let me ask you in respect of these exhibits, if you would have the map on the ELMO, could you orient the Judges to the location where the Drina Corps 5th Engineering Battalion was located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The location of the 5th Engineering Battalion is very close to the so-called intersection of Konjevici, where the red circle is. It is approximately 800 metres -- or 600 metres away from the intersection. The road on the right is the road leading towards Bratunac town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Would you take the next exhibit, please, Mr. Ruez, 160/1, and place that on the ELMO. I'm going to interrupt you once or twice in your testimony about this location, but I'd like you now to use those exhibits, starting with 160/1 through 160/8, and slowly identify the significance of each of these images, and tell the Judges about each of these exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is an aerial photograph taken the 27th of July, 1995 which shows the large area around the compound of the 5th Engineering. The HQ is in the middle of the photograph. The surroundings are buildings, and this is the road going from Bratunac, which is at the right of the photograph, towards the intersection of Konjevici, which is just out of the frame of the picture on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the road that starts at the upper right-hand side of the image, and at approximately a 45-degree angle descends to the left lower portion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is correct. This picture is broken into three frames, frame A, frame B, and frame C. I'm going to show now additional pictures from these frames.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, excuse me. Can I interrupt to ask the technical booth to give us an overall view of all these photographs, please, together. I can't see the top of the photograph, please. I should like to see the whole thing, please. Put the photograph under the ELMO, and whenever one puts a document on the ELMO I would like us to be able to see the whole photograph. Does the technical booth understand what I'm saying? Could you focus it so that the whole photograph can be seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This photograph, Mr. President, may be too large to -- I think it's an A3-size photograph. I'm not sure if this ELMO can show all of the picture in one shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That way it could work but it's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. Harmon. We've seen the whole photograph now and you may continue. I apologise for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Continue, please, Mr. Ruez. Why don't you take the next image and tell Their Honours what 160/2 is. Did you take this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The photograph that I took on the 8th April 1996, this is a photograph of the headquarters of the 5th Engineer Unit. It is in a former school. This is the building in the centre of the photograph, and to the left of the photograph is the guardhouse. This guardhouse is the guardhouse which was identified by (redacted). He was taken to that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Then continue, please, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The Exhibit 160/3 is a blowup of frame A of the larger photograph that was the Exhibit 161.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That has to be better oriented on the ELMO, Mr. Ruez, and if you can get the whole image in.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photograph was taken on the 5th of July, 1995. The markings in white are the original markings we received on this photograph from the State Department, the U.S. State Department. The markings in yellow are additional markings that we have added on these photographs according to the knowledge we have of what can be seen on it. These vehicles that can be seen on this photograph, 5 July 1995, are mobile bridge trucks. The photograph Exhibit 160/4 shows these bridge trucks still present there on the 8th April 1996. It is to enable you to compare ground picture with aerial imagery in order to have a better view of what the objects on the photographs represent. So on the 5th July 1995, only these mobile bridge trucks were present in the compound. The next exhibit, which is 160/5, is a photograph from the same area taken 27 July 1995, and one can observe that in addition to the mobile bridge trucks, a front loader has arrived at the 5th Engineer Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "165," you mean "160/5," for the record?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Correct. Exhibit 160/6 is a blowup of frame B of the initial exhibit. The first photograph is dated July 5, and one can see on the photograph a tractor and a trailer. The Exhibit 160/7 shows the same area on the 27th of July, 1995. In addition to the trailer and the tractor still present on the 27th of July, 1995, two trucks arrived and one additional front loader. Exhibit 160/8 is a blowup of frame C of the Exhibit 160/1. It just shows what was present there on the 5th of July, 1995. The next photograph is 160/9. No equipment is to be seen on this photograph, no additional equipment, besides the vehicle which was already present there on 5 July, but there was some additional activity in this area due to traces on the ground in this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "traces," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Vehicle traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point those out to the Judges, please?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: In the centre of the picture, in this area here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this particular engineering company, is this part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is a Drina Corps unit, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. I've concluded then, Mr. Ruez, with those particular exhibits about the Engineering Unit, and if we could now turn to two exhibits that have been previously entered in through Captain Egberg's testimony, Prosecutor's Exhibit 87 and 88. Now, Mr. Ruez, the Dutch soldier who testified before the Tribunal, Captain Egberg, testified that he was at this particular location near Nova Kasaba. First of all, can you identify in this aerial image the location of the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The 65th Protection Regiment was billeting in a school just on the outskirts of the hamlet of Nova Kasaba, and the school building, which is the headquarters of the 65th Protection Regiment in July 1995, is the building at the bottom of this picture. In front of it one can see that three buses are present 13 July 1995 at 1400 hours, and the path that exits the compound is the straight line going toward the road which is on the upper right corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In which direction is Nova Kasaba when you're on the road in the upper right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Nova Kasaba is in the direction of the road which exits the photo at the top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can we take a look at the next exhibit, Prosecutor's Exhibit 87 -- 88, I'm sorry. Captain Egberg identified this particular location. What is this location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the same school that shall be seen on the aerial imagery. It is the compound of the 65th Protection Regiment. It's a photograph which was taken in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I've finished with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, I'm going to show you a video film. It will be brief. It will be -- it's Exhibit 66, and it is an interview with General Krstic. I'm going to ask you some questions after you've had an opportunity to look at the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if we could dim the lights, please, and if we could show Prosecutor's Exhibit 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, do you know when this film was shown publicly and where it was shown?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This film was broadcasted on Serbian news, which is VRS Television, the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, we've had another witness in this court look at this film, Colonel Kingori, and Colonel Kingori concluded that that film was taken in Potocari. Do you agree with Colonel Kingori's conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with Major Kingori's conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many times, approximately, have you been to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I did not count them, but I would say probably ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like you to use four exhibits, and show the Court, if you would, why you agree with Colonel Kingori.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 5/4, 5/19 [realtime transcript read in error "5/15"], 5/5. We need them in an ensemble so we can go through this testimony fairly quickly. You can place 5/4 on the ELMO. We won't start your testimony yet, Mr. Ruez. We'll wait until we have the exhibits before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. You mentioned "5/19" or did you say "5/15"?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I said, "5/5, 5/19, 5/4," and then we have a new exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 184.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: Because the transcript says "5/15".

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And there's a new exhibit, 184. If that 184 could be distributed, then I'll start the examination of Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, if you would identify, by number, the exhibits when you testify about them. I would like you to take the Chamber through these exhibits, and tell them why this last interview of General Krstic was taken in Potocari, why you have reached that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph dated 13 July 1995, taken at 1400 hours. It shows the situation in Potocari at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The exhibit number on that, please?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The exhibit number of this one is 5/4. In the centre of the picture, one can see in the circle a crowd of people. These are people waiting to board the buses and have to go through the separation line before doing so. The separation line is here [indicates], more or less in the middle of the photograph. On the film where General Krstic can be seen giving his interview, at one point a blue building is visible in the frame. The blue building is the building which is marked on the photograph, with the arrow, "Blue Building." The approximate location of the interview was just before reaching the separation line, when coming from Bratunac, which is in the direction of the bottom of this photograph. The area where the interview took place is approximately here [indicates] on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which is below the oval and to the right of the word that says "Trucks"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May we have the next exhibit, please, 5/19.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is another view of the area seen from the west. In the centre, a bit to the right, is the so-called blue building [indicates]. Just behind this blue building is the asphalt road that goes right off the picture towards Srebrenica town [indicates]. Just outside the frame of this photograph is the area where the separation line was [indicates]. And behind the house which is at the right of the photograph centre picture is the approximate area where the interview was taken, due to the angle where the building can be seen, the blue building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could now turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/5. Place that on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is again another view from Potocari, but seen from the east. The blue building on this photograph is now on the top right of the photo [indicates]. It is not blue on this digital photograph. The building is here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You're indicating, for the record, the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, just before the so-called "white house," which was the detention centre for the men who were separated. On the left of this blue building, one can see a big group of trees. Just behind these trees is the approximate area where the interview took place. This interview, which was broadcast on 13 July, was in fact given 12 July, 12 July, probably around noon or very early -- around noon, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the last image, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 184, and explain this image to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph extracted from a video that we took in Potocari, the 1st of June, 1996. If one would extract from the video of the interview given by General Krstic a still photograph, one could notice on that photograph the top right windows of this blue building, as well as the electrical pylons which are visible behind the building. The approximate area where the interview took place is on this dotted line where these two arrows are at the right of the photograph. Most probably where the arrow is, which is closest to the right frame of the photograph, was the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you a still image from that interview. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 158. Mr. Ruez, over General Krstic's left shoulder there's an image of a man in the background with a full front face. Can you identify that man, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The man that can be seen just behind General Krstic is Colonel Vujadin Popovic, the Chief of Security for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Also, sorry, this is a picture also where one can see on the top right, you can see a bit of a blue structure with -- on top of it, it's very shady on this photograph, but this probably should be one of the two pylons which were visible on the previous exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you keep that photo on the ELMO, please, Mr. Usher, and if you could now get Prosecutor's Exhibits 28/8 and 28/8.1 [Realtime transcript read in error "128 and 128/8.1"].

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: On this still there is a truck just behind General Krstic that hides the view of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The man you have identified as Popovic in this particular image, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 58, I'd like to show you two new exhibits -- two older exhibits, 28/8 and 28/8.1, and ask you if this is the same man who appears in Prosecutor's Exhibit 58. So if we could place 28/8 on the ELMO. Is that the same man who appeared behind General Krstic on the 12th of July in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same man. He looks a little bit younger on this photograph, which was extracted from news footage dated 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could now put the next image on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is an image that was taken on the 11th of July in Srebrenica. The man on the left-hand side, in a brown T-shirt, carrying what looks like an automatic weapon in his left hand, is that the same man who appeared behind General Krstic in the interview on the 12th of July in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The man on the left of the photograph, in a T-shirt, carrying an AK-47, is again Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, we've covered the first part of your testimony, which is essentially to connect various pieces of evidence with your knowledge. I'd now like to turn to the principal part of your testimony and the reason why you were called back to testify. During the first part of your testimony, which was extensive, you identified for the Trial Chamber a number of locations that were relevant to this particular indictment. Now we're going to go to the second chapter, if you will, in respect of many of those sites; that is, I'm going to ask you to identify various locations where mass graves are located, where people who were executed were buried. I'm going to ask you to first of all orient the Judges by using Prosecutor's Exhibit 187 to those locations and then I'm going to ask you some additional questions after you orient the Judges and the gallery to these locations. If you would, Mr. Ruez, would you identify the primary mass grave sites and the secondary mass grave sites.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So this map is another map of the crime scene of the Srebrenica case which has the specificity to have the relief marked on it. The relief is fairly accurate with the exception that Udrc Mountain on this map doesn't seem as high as it is. For the rest, it is an accurate representation of the relief of the area. The relief is a very important aspect in this operation. A normal map would be less clear in terms of showing how remote some of these places can be. Going from north to south -- the symbols also are different from the first map that you got as an exhibit during my initial testimony -- going from north to south, the primary mass graves on this map are marked with a triangle and two bodies in it. This is the marking for a primary mass grave. So in the north we have the Branjevo Farm. There is another symbol with an excavator in it meaning that the site is a disturbed site. In this area north, the second mass grave that was identified is the mass grave of Kozluk. That is marked with a triangle with two bodies in it. It is also a site that has been disturbed which is the reason why the excavator symbol is next to the mass grave. The site of Petkovci is also marked on this map as an execution site, mass grave, and disturbed mass grave, with the symbol of the excavator. The situation is the same for the Orahovac mass grave which has also the symbol of disturbance next to it. In the area south are also several mass graves. The primary mass grave at Glogova, here on the map, has also been disturbed. The symbol of the excavator is next to it. But in the area of Konjevici, there is a cluster of several graves. None of these graves have been disturbed. The reason could be the release of the aerial photographs in August 1995 to the United Nations and the public. The other additional reason could be also the limited amount of bodies that could be found -- that are in these locations. We found out later, having completed the exhumations, that just above 100 bodies were exhumed in the three graves in the area of Nova Kasaba. The grave in the valley of Cerska is also a non-disturbed site. The reason could be similar to the one for the no disturbance of the Nova Kasaba sites, due to the proximity of the Cancari valley site. An additional explanation could be also the limited amount -- the relative limited amount of people that were present in this grave, since about 150 bodies were recovered in this one which is not a huge number compared with the number of people executed in the area north. The third explanation could be that this area is a very remote valley, as you could see on the video film from the helicopter which was presented during my first testimony. The symbols for the secondary mass graves, which are the result of a disturbance of primary ones, are yellow triangles with only one individual inside. You can clearly notice on this photograph, on this exhibit, that in the area north are three clusters of secondary sites: One along the road that we call the Hodzici road; we name it according to one of the villages, destroyed villages, which is along this dirt road. Another cluster is in the area of the village of Liplje, which is also an area of destroyed villages which were previously occupied by a Muslim population in 1992. The third cluster of secondary sites in the area north is the so-called Cancari road. We picked the name "Cancari" because it is also one of the names of the villages along this road. The main village in this area is Kamenica so everyone would refer to that by the name Kamenica. We couldn't do that for the reason that we already had used this name to name the ambush that took place south of Kravica on the 13th of July, 1995. So we did not use that name twice and called this valley the Cancari Valley. The last cluster of secondary sites is to be found just at the south of the Srebrenica former enclave, in the area of Zeleni Jadar, which is at the bottom of this exhibit. The only little problem with this exhibit is that the approximate boundary of the enclave is marked on it, as well as the observation posts which are in yellow colour and can create a little confusion with the cluster of sites in Zeleni Jadar. So please just disregard these OPs for the sake of understanding this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you used the word "disturbance" in your testimony. Do you mean that bodies were taken from the primary mass grave sites, dug up, transported, and reburied in the secondary sites which are marked with yellow triangles?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely. The secondary sites are the result of a disturbance of the primary ones, and the bodies which were inside the primary graves, except those that were forgotten during this transfer process and that were later found in the primary sites, all the rest of these bodies have been scattered in these numerous secondary sites, most probably with the intent that we would not find them, and even if we would find just a few of them, the content of these sites is always between 80 -- approximately 80 and 180 individuals. Therefore, it would never be a representation of the number of people who had been assassinated in cold blood during all this process.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before we end with this particular exhibit, let me ask you: Are all the primary mass grave sites and the secondary mass grave sites depicted on this exhibit located within the Drina Corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. All these sites are within the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps, and later on this map will have to be, in a way, overlaid on top of a map that will represent the areas of responsibilities of the various units that were present in this zone in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You can have a seat, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, my colleague has inform me that the record may be inaccurate insofar as Prosecutor's Exhibits 28/8 and 28/8.1, the pictures of Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. I think it may show on the record that it was 128 reflected, and the proper reference, so the record can be corrected, of the two images I showed Mr. Ruez are 28/8 and 28/8.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, now I'd like you to develop for the Trial Chamber the evidence showing that the primary mass grave sites were disturbed and the possible dates of those disturbances. I would also like you to develop the dates when the secondary grave sites were created. You should have before you a series of exhibits from 161, ending with 169, and if you would start with the primary -- let's start with the primary sites, Mr. Ruez. Let's start with the primary site of Glogova, and if you would use those exhibits, please, and give the Judges of this Trial Chamber the evidence that relates to that particular site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit 161/A is the map of the area of Bratunac and Glogova. The two red dots on this map mark the location of the Glogova sites. The Glogova site is, in fact, separated in two; one that we name Glogova 1 and the second one that we called Glogova 2. These are grave sites. It doesn't mean that on each site is only one grave. Exhibit 161/1 shows the situation on the ground in the village of -- former village, I mean, destroyed village of Glogova, the 27th of July, 1995. We already showed the photographs linked with the creation of this mass grave site. This is the situation on the ground on the 27th of July, 1995 where the exhumation is completed on both sites. Exhibit 161/2 is a view of the site code-named GL-1, Glogova 1. This is after the exhumation has been conducted. I mean, this is a picture of 1996 when everything is already over there. But this is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, when you say "after the exhumation has been conducted," are you referring to the exhumation by the Office of the Prosecutor or are you referring to an exhumation by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photograph is dated 1996, so it is in fact the area after the initial burial and then after the disturbance. So this one is just to indicate how the area looked like at the site Glogova 1, and the destruction also of the village. The Exhibit 161/3 is the ground view of the site Glogova 2, which, as one can see, is close to a former Muslim cemetery. That photograph was already shown. The Exhibit 161/4 shows the site Glogova 1. The photograph on the left is dated 27 July 1995, and all the parts which are white versus all the rest of the picture which is dark black is the area of disturbed soil after the initial burial. The picture on the right of this photograph is dated 20 October 1995. It is quite dark, but one can see on this photograph an excavator present on the site, as well as a deep trench which is going across this site. So there was an open pit created there on the 20th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this is an aerial image of the disturbance, in other words, the removal of bodies that were initially deposited in this site being removed.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. At this date, 20 October 1995, either the work is still in progress since the excavator is still there, or the bodies have already been taken out of this site and the excavator is probably soon going to redump soil inside this empty hole and recreate a flat surface there. Exhibit 161/5 is an aerial photograph, dated 30 October 1995, that shows that the site Glogova 1 is finished in terms of disturbance, or the disturbance of that site is done, but the site Glogova 2 is still under disturbance. The same situation: either the disturbance is already over and the bodies have already been taken away but the presence of the front loader in the hole could indicate there is still work ongoing, or that this excavator, front loader, is now going to redump the soil in the hole in order to reflatten all this area. The Exhibit 161/6 is a photograph of this same area showing the two sites. On the right of the photograph is the site Glogova 1 and on the left, the site Glogova 2. This is a photograph in wintertime, the ground is covered by snow, and there is nothing that could indicate to anyone that something had happened here if we did not have the previous pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when the Office of the Prosecutor conducted exhumations at these sites, did they also find evidence that these sites had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We won't go into detail, that will be the subject of additional testimony by witnesses who will be testifying after you, but I just wanted to have you confirm that fact.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. My colleague Dean Manning will give you all the details about the findings inside these graves, disturbed or not disturbed, and will provide all the details regarding the connection of these sites, each with another.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, have you finished your development of the evidence in respect of this particular site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. For Glogova, the presentation is done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 162, please, which is the primary mass grave site at Orahovac. Again, Mr. Ruez, if you would take the exhibits in sequence and develop for the Trial Chamber the history of that particular site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 162/A is the map of the area, and the circle marks the approximate location of the Orahovac primary mass grave site. The Exhibit 162/1 is a photograph that I took on the 26th of April, 1997 in the hamlet of Lazete. It shows two things: One, the aim of this photograph is to show this sign where, at the bottom of it, is written in Cyrillic, "Orahovac," so that confirms the name of this area. It will have some importance in the future. In fact, the sign invites people in fact to go to a restaurant which is on the right-hand side of this photograph. Just behind that sign is a white building which is what one witness thinks is a railway station, and he hid in this railway station just after having escaped from the execution alive. He walked on the railway tracks and reached that location. This is just very close to the Grbovci school. Exhibit 162/2 shows the Orahovac execution sites and mass grave sites. The photograph at the left is dated 5 July 1995. There is nothing special to be seen on it. At the left of the picture is the road that, if one exits the picture at the top, leads to the Grbovci school. That was the detention site for the prisoners. The little path that turns right is the dirt track that then goes under the underpass of the railroad and reaches the execution site which was used initially. On the photograph dated 27 July 1995, one can see the result of the burial activity of the victims of these executions, with one massive disturbance at the bottom of the photo. That was the first execution site used for the prisoners that were kept at the Grbovci school. At the top of the photo is the second execution area, and most probably also a burial site, where a disturbance is clearly noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 27th of July, this shows where the victims of this mass execution were buried; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, this is the initial burial location. Exhibit 162/3 is a helicopter view of these two sites. At the bottom of the photograph is the site number 1. This area here, it was a disturbed area on the aerial imagery. The other site, which is site number 2, is just at the top right of the house that is in the middle of the picture, and it is the area where the second area of disturbed soil can be seen on the aerial photograph. That marks the presence of a secondary mass grave there. Exhibit 162/4 shows the site 1. The picture at the left is dated 7 September 1995; it shows how the ground looks on that date. The photograph on the right is dated 27 September 1995; it shows the same spot of the ground and one can notice that the area of disturbance has changed. The area of disturbed soil is larger than on the photograph dated the 7th of September. So on 27 September, the exhumation of the primary site was completed and the bodies have been removed from this site. As you will hear later on, not all of the bodies had been removed. Some were forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this is the smaller of the two sites at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: We cannot say that. It is the first site that was used, so most probably it is the bigger one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: At some point, the meadow was completely covered with bodies, so the execution was switched to the other site, which is LZ-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 162/5 is aerial imagery of the second site of Orahovac which we call LZ-2. So the photograph on the left shows the ground at the date of 7 September 1995. At the top of the picture, one can see the railroad line. I made a mistake. I mixed the two, in fact. The comment that I was making for the previous one is for this one. This is the site number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this is the larger?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, because site number 2 on the markings, in fact it is the reverse in terms of the happenings for the executions. The executions first happened on the site that we mark LZ-2 and then continued on the site that we mark LZ-1. We discovered, in fact, this change of chronology when we brought the witnesses back on the crime scene. The reason is that the victims inside the gymnasium never refer hearing about -- hearing the shooting that is happening approximately 800 metres -- only 800 metres away from the gymnasium. We realised the reason why when we went on the spot with the survivors. The reason could be that there is a very quite high elevation of ground to support the railroad, and this makes a kind of natural sound barrier. So most probably if you add the fact that the people were talking a little bit in another -- in the gymnasium, all this would come as rumours. And the soldiers were shooting from time to time above their heads, hitting the windows. This was probably also making their ears buzzing, and they probably didn't hear what was going on during the executions on the first site. But unfortunately once the execution was switched on the second site, most probably those inside the gymnasium could hear what was happening, and then probably this had some consequences on their conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the significance of this photograph, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This photograph, which is the LZ-2 site, but that is the first execution site used on the 14th July 1995. On the left photograph, dated 7 September, one can see the disturbed soil which is of a white colour on this photograph, and on the right is a photograph dated the 27th September, and the area of disturbance is clearly larger than the one dated 7 September, indicating that something happened there. The exhumation confirmed, indeed, that disturbance happened here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you wish to say anything else, Mr. Ruez, about the Orahovac site or should we move to --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, we are moving on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again if you develop the evidence about the disturbances that took place at the Dam at Petkovci, the location of the mass execution.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 163/A is the map of the area nearby Zvornik town and Kakanj, and the circle marks the location of the plateau of the Dam where the execution took place and the burial of part of the victims; probably not all of the victims, since we don't know what happened with the victims that were -- corpses of the victims that were transported away by the little trailer. Exhibit 163/1 is a helicopter view from the Dam, and the arrow at the right of the photograph shows the location of the disturbed soil where a mass grave was. Exhibit 163/2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this is a before-and-after shot, is it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Explain the "before" and explain the "after."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So 5 July 1995, the photograph at the left of this picture shows the Dam, the plateau of the Dam, and 5 July is before events, so there is nothing specific to be seen there. We know that the execution at the Dam took place on 14 July 1995. The photograph at the right of this picture is dated 27 July 1995, and it shows an obvious area of recently-disturbed gravel. In fact, there is no soil there. It is rocks. That was the creation of the primary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So that's where at least some of the victims of that mass execution were initially buried?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the initial burial site. And on Exhibit 163/3, one can again see how the ground looked like on the 7th of September, 1995. That is the part -- the left part of this picture. And for comparison, the right part of the picture dated 27 July 1995 shows that the area looks slightly different. The fact is that here the photograph is obviously not taken at the same moment of the day. The photograph at the left is probably taken around noon, and the one on the right, later in the afternoon, so the shadows are very different on these two photographs. That weakens the comparison, but we can confirm that indeed the disturbance took place there because an exhumation was conducted, and the results showed that indeed it was a mass grave. And it was no more a mass grave when we did the exhumation because the bodies had been taken away, but body parts were forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sometime prior to the 27th of September, 1995, the bodies were removed from each location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. From this photograph, the only conclusion we can draft is that the disturbance took place at some point between 7 September 1995 and 27 September 1995. I must add also that all this is work in progress and that we might be able, in the future, to narrow down a bit better these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Why don't we turn to another primary mass grave site, the primary mass grave site found at Kozluk. If you would start with exhibits found in tab 164.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 164/A is the map of the area of Kozluk, and the red circle marks the position of -- approximate position of the mass grave -- of the execution site and mass grave of Kozluk. In fact, it is very close to the Drina River, so it is not a very accurate marking on this exhibit. The Exhibit 164/1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a before-and-after shot, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is a before-and-after shot of the area of the execution site and initial burial site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you explain, Mr. Ruez, the "before" and the "after"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Umm-hmm. The left part of these photographs shows -- completely on the left, the Drina River. And on the right part, it's an area of sand creeks. So there had already been disturbed soil, but this disturbed soil is linked with the dumping of garbage and broken glass from the Betinka [phoen] factory, as we know, but also because people go in this location to take gravel out of these sand creeks. The photograph dated 17 July 1995 shows that the area has significantly been changed. We know that the execution took place on this location, and here the burial of the victims is completed. There is an open trench that is visible at the left of the photograph [indicates], the photograph that is on the right of this picture. Again, you can see, just at the left edge, the Drina River and one open pit [indicates]. In fact, this open pit is not there to put bodies, but it has been used to take soil and cover the bodies which are, in fact, buried to the right of this open pit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So on this image, on the 5th of July, the executions had not yet taken place, and therefore there is no major disturbance of the soil. And on the right-hand side, after the executions took place, one can see on this image the soil has been disturbed and it's significantly different; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Exhibit 164/2 is a helicopter view of the area. That was -- that photograph was presented during my first testimony, and I present it again to make a correction. This is, in fact, not the mass grave site. The mass grave site is just at the left of this photograph. If one exits from the path that is just here in the middle of the picture at the left [indicates], then just a few metres after this, one hits the mass grave area. This area here [indicates] is in fact disconnected from the execution burial site. It is an area of gravel. Just a confusion on the very precise location. But that photograph still gives a very good view on how close the river is and also of how the terrain looks like and the cornfields around. That also matched the information that we got on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's go to the imagery that shows the disturbance of this primary mass grave, which is in Prosecutor's Exhibit 164/3.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That exhibit again shows, at the left of this photograph, the situation on the ground dated 7 September 1995, so after the initial burial was concluded. And the photograph on the right, dated 27 September 1995, shows that the soil has significantly changed at that location. That change on the ground is linked with the disturbance of the site where excavators came and unburied a certain number of bodies there. The usual amount was forgotten, as my colleague will explain when he will testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Without going into any detail, there was evidence, then, at the subsequent exhumation conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor that this site had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The exhumation conducted there confirmed that indeed it was an execution site, an initial burial site, and that then the site was disturbed and bodies taken in an unknown direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Ruez, let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 165 and the subsequent sub-parts of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This deals with the Branjevo Military Farm, and Your Honours have heard testimony about a mass execution that took place at the Branjevo Military Farm through the testimony of Drazen Erdemovic and survivors.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 165/A is the map of the area. Right in the middle of the right circle are the buildings of the Branjevo Farm. We can see three dots that mark the buildings. Exhibit 165/1 is a helicopter view photograph taken in 1996 of these buildings. So in the middle of the photograph is the Branjevo Farm, and that picture shows also the surroundings. The execution site is at the right of the photograph just after passing the little shed behind which the executioners were staying. And on the right part of the photograph is the execution field. The area where the initial burial took place is also visible on the photo. It is the little white area completely at the right of the photograph, more or less in the middle [indicates]. Exhibit 165/2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This photograph is taken the day after the executions took place at the Branjevo Military Farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The execution there took place 16 July 1995, and this is the picture that we already showed taken 17 July 1995, where bodies can be seen on the ground; not all the bodies, because many of them have already been taken away by that time. One can see the traces of the excavator that collected these bodies on the soil, and one can see also the burial area where the exhumation is ongoing at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point out the area where the bodies are located?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Where it is written at the left of the picture: "Access ramp to mass grave," just underneath is the area where the grave was. Just at the edge of the grave is also a certain number of dots that are suspected bodies [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And where are the principal killing fields? Can you point that out.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. On this photograph, the area that is encircled here only shows where the bodies are. The execution -- the site of the execution field was larger than that. It covers, in fact, all the area where vehicle traces can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the Court has heard testimony from Mr. Erdemovic that approximately 1.200 people were killed at this location on the 16th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, please, will you continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
