utterances.text: The photograph of the same farm taken the 21st of September, 1995, shows that the burial area that we had just been pointing at, which is more or less at the same location on this photograph [indicates] at the bottom left, is untouched. So this is the situation on the ground on the 21st September 1995, after everything is completed there. The initial burial is over, and for the moment the situation here is stable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This photograph, Mr. Ruez, is the "before" image, then, of the disturbance from the primary mass grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this next image, what does this show, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The next picture shows the situation after.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the next picture is 165/4.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is dated 27 September 1995. It again shows the farm, and at the location where the grave is to be found, there is a newly-excavated trench. So most probably 27 July 1995, the bodies have already been taken out of that initial burial location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So sometime, Mr. Ruez, between the 21st of September and the 27th of September, there was a disturbance at that mass grave site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely. We cannot conclude that the excavation is completed at that moment, but it is the best frame of the date that we can have at this moment. On this photograph also, there is a blowup of the central part of the picture. The site is small, but there is a backhoe and a front loader present at the Branjevo Farm at that moment. So probably the equipment that was used to do the disturbance and take the bodies away from the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So a backhoe and a front loader are heavy construction equipment that would be used to excavate the soil, and collect the bodies, and put them into trucks to transport them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is correct. It is two types of equipment that we will constantly see again in action on these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Ruez, I think that completes our tour of the primary mass grave sites. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now what I would like you to do is focus your attention on the secondary grave sites, in other words, the locations where bodies were taken from these primary sites, concealed, and reburied. Why don't we start --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this is a good time for the break. In that case, we'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will resume the hearing. Mr. Harmon, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, just before the break you had concluded your discussion about disturbances at the primary mass grave sites, and I'd now like to turn your attention to disturbances or the creation of the secondary mass grave sites and the clusters of those sites. I'd like you to first of all turn your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 166, the cluster of secondary mass grave sites as Zeleni Jadar. Before you begin your testimony, using the large map to your right, using the pointer, could you just point out that particular cluster about which you're going to be testifying.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The cluster of secondary sites of Zeleni Jadar is just at the south of the former Srebrenica safe area, and it is just at the bottom right of the map exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, using the exhibits that are found in Prosecutor's Exhibit 166 and following, could you testify about the creation of those sites, each specific site, and if you can identify before-and-after shots as "before" and "after" shots and if you could also identify the dates that are relevant to each of these images.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. The first exhibit is number 166/A. It is the map of the area of Srebrenica. The green dots mark the precise position of these secondary mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So there are six in total at this location.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: There are six sites in total. As we will see, one of these sites is, in fact, consisting of two graves. Exhibit 166/1 is a large photograph, an overview of all the area of Zeleni Jadar. It cannot go completely under the ELMO so I will have it like this. This shows the terrain in Zeleni Jadar. It is a rough terrain of hills. It is a very remote area; nearly no one is living in this place. It's a complete trashed zone; it was a former combat zone. There is no one living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It looks heavily wooded.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It is heavily wooded, and it is also heavily mined. There are several Bosnian Serb army minefields in this area, and the choice of this area is probably linked with the presence of these minefields since even locals would probably be deterred to go wandering in this area. So this map shows the position on the ground of all these secondary mass graves, and we will now present them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you just, while you have that image before you and before the Judges, just indicate ZJ-1. I take that is the location of the first secondary mass grave side.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct. The coding "ZJ" stands for Zeleni Jadar, and "1" is the site number 1 which is the most north, and then the numbering goes from north to south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you just move that image completely across the ELMO so all of the sites can eventually be seen.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Site number 6 is the most south.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 166/2 is a before-and-after photograph of the area where the site Zeleni Jadar 1 is located. On the left of the picture one can see the shape of the ground at the date of 7 September 1995, and on the picture on the right one can see that there is an open pit, which is marked with a yellow arrow, and that is Zeleni Jadar 1. The photograph is dated 2 October 1995, so at that date there was just an open pit created there but nothing inside. A bit further down on this photograph -- that is the reason why I said that in this location there is probably more than one site -- you can also see that there is an open pit a bit more south of the Zeleni Jadar 1 grave. We cannot count this site as a grave at this moment because we could not access this place due to the mine threat in this location, so it will be probably done but at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, so what we know from this image is sometime between the 7th of September, 1995 and the 2nd of October, 1995 these secondary mass grave sites were created.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Between this time frame, an open pit is created. For the moment it is still not a mass grave. For the moment it is just an open pit. One can notice also the size of these pits. There is no reference in size, but it's approximately a tank size. You could probably enter this position with a tank. So there is no reason to suspect such a hole there. That could be very well something like a defensive position. The fact is at that time there was no need at all to create defensive positions in this location since on the 2nd of October, 1995 the enclave was already eradicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why don't you show the next image and show the Judges what happened at this location at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 166/3 shows again the same area, but now the picture on the left is dated 18 October 1995. The same open pit is visible on the photograph. So the situation between 2 October 1995 and 18 October 1995 is unchanged. The same open pit south of Zeleni Jadar 1 is also still open. On the right of the photograph, at the date 20 October 1995, Zeleni Jadar 1 is now a filled grave and the suspect hole south of Zeleni Jadar 1 is filled as well. The site had been probed, and it is indeed a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which site has been probed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The Zeleni Jadar 1 site has been probed only so far. So one can conclude from these photographs that between 18 October 1995 and 20 October 1995 the site was filled with bodies. Now we're moving on to Zeleni Jadar 2 site, which is Exhibit 166/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Exhibit 166/4.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: "/4." It is also a before-and-after shot. The "before" shot is dated 24 August 1995. It shows, in fact, only the gravel road. At the bottom of the picture is a wooded hill, at the bottom of which is a little river flowing. The picture on the right is dated 7 October 1995, and one can observe that between 24 August and the 2nd of October, an open pit was created there as well. At this moment the pit is probably filled with water which is coming from the little brook which is running there. Exhibit 166/5 is a more fuzzy photograph but it still shows that at 20 October 1995 the Zeleni Jadar 2 site is still an open pit, it is not filled. So the situation has not changed between 23 October -- sorry, between the previous one, between the 2nd of October and the 20th of October. But between 20 October and 23 October 1995, that is the picture on the right of this present exhibit, that one can see that the Zeleni Jadar site 2 is filled. An additional comment on this site is that we found out during the exhumation of this site that it was a disturbed site. This is the only disturbed secondary site that we have encountered so far. We have no reasonable explanation that could explain what happened. There is still something that could be double-checked. There could be a pumping station in this location of Zeleni Jadar using the water from that brook and then this water is allegedly pumped to bring water to Srebrenica town. So it might very well be that these bodies here will have polluted the water table and therefore they had to be taken away at a later stage. But we do not have the explanation of why this secondary site was later on disturbed, and we do not know when the disturbance took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So by "disturbed," you mean the bodies in this secondary site were removed and located some place else.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Ruez. Go to the next before-and-after shot.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 166/6 is a before-and-after photograph of the site that we name Zeleni Jadar 3. On the picture dated 7 September 1995, on the left of the screen, one can see the ground before a change occurs, and at 2 October 1995, one can see that there is an open hole which is marked on this photograph with yellow markers "Zeleni Jadar 3." The next photograph is the same site. It is the Exhibit 166/7. The photograph is a bit fuzzy but still shows that at 20 October 1995 the hole does not exist any more; it has been filled. The site has been probed and contains multiple remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So between the 2nd of October, 1995 and the 20th of October, 1995 the hole was filled with human remains.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: With human remains, absolutely. The following exhibit is 166/8. It shows two sites that are in the vicinity of each other. The photograph at the top of this picture is dated 7 September 1995 and shows nothing special. Compared with the photograph dated 12 October 1995, one can observe that there are two open pits created in that location, so created between 7 September and 12 October. One is code-named Zeleni Jadar 4 and the second one is Zeleni Jadar 5. We will mark on the picture 7 September where these sites are because the photograph is taken from another angle and this transforms the landscape a bit. The Zeleni Jadar 5 site -- this does not work -- the Zeleni Jadar 5 site is in that location and Zeleni Jadar 4, on the photograph dated 7 September, would be where I put the second arrow, which is here. So a slightly different perspective than the photograph dated 2 October 1995. In 12 October 1995, so we have open pits in these locations, and the next exhibit, which is 166/9, is also a photograph that is a bit fuzzy but one can still see on this one that both the site Zeleni Jadar 4 and the site Zeleni Jadar 5 are now filled. These sites were -- Zeleni Jadar 4 site was probed and contains multiple human remains, and Zeleni Jadar site 5 has been fully exhumed and the results of this exhumation will be developed by my colleague Dean Manning, as well as the connection between this site and some primary one. The next exhibit is 166/10 and shows a before-and-after photograph of the site number 6. One can see that at 7 September 1995 there is nothing special on the ground, but at 27 September 1995 there is a big trench, big open trench, that can be seen in that location. So that site was created -- that open pit was created between 7 September and 27 September. Exhibit 166/11 shows the same terrain, this time dated 12 October 1995, the picture on the left side. It is quite unclear to determine at what stage this site is at this moment. It is obvious that the site is no more an open trench but it is still not -- the work is still not completed there, since at 18 October 1995 one can see that there is a large area of disturbed soil on that same spot where previously there was an open trench. So the conclusion we can draw here is that it is only for sure 18 October 1995 -- at some point between 12 October 1995 and 18 October 1995 that the work was completed on this site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, has that site been probed or exhumed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The site has been probed and the presence of multiple remains was found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, does that complete your review of the secondary sites at Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is correct. So we have six confirmed secondary sites in Zeleni Jadar, and a potential number 7 grave which could be, in fact, the one just south of the site number 1. We will determine that probably this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I'd like you to focus your attention on the cluster of secondary sites now at the Hodzici road. Would you again begin by pointing out on the large map where that cluster of secondary grave sites is located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The Hodzici sites are just at the west of Zvornik town. It is a dirt road that goes from Zvornik to the national road that then goes to Tuzla. It's a dirt road. It's an area of destroyed villages formally occupied by Muslims in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, is this also an isolated area that's heavily wooded?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, the same situation, with a difference with the others, which are mainly in valleys. This one is along a road which follows a hill line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ruez, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So regarding these sites, the Exhibit 167/A is the map of the area, and the green dots mark the precise position of seven sites which have been found and probed and confirmed as mass graves containing human remains. Some of them have been fully exhumed. Exhibit 167/1 is an aerial photograph -- a mosaic of several photographs reconstructing the so-called Hodzici road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you explain the coding, please, on the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. So all the sites we have worked on are marked on this photograph, starting with HZ-1 -- that stands for Hodzici 1 -- through Hodzici 7, with very precise spot marking where these graves are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, on the caption on the lower right-hand image, it says "Cerik Road Segment." The other two captions say "Hodzici Road Segment." Just for the record, will you explain the difference, please?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The difference comes from the titles that were given to these photographs from the US State Department, who provided us these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But for purposes of this testimony, all of these sites are referred to as the Hodzici road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. Cerik is the village closest from the graves Hodzici 6 and Hodzici 7. The reason why? On that photograph initially, the area was not just Cerik but was also closer to Hodzici, which is why they were named "Hodzici." For us, we named the entire road "Hodzici."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. With that clarification, please continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 167/2 is a photograph of soil, dated 7 September 1995, where a grave will be created later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Ruez, this is a location -- a "before" shot of the location where Hodzici 1 or 2 is located?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is a photograph where the site 2 will be located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The site 1 -- I have to confirm -- correct something. Site 1 has been trenched, probed, and was negative. The site 1 does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. With that clarification, then, please continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the second exhibit is number 167/3 and shows the same terrain but dated 7 October 1995, showing that in between the 7 September 1995 and that date, 7 October 1995, an area of disturbed soil can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You mean "2 October 1995," not "7"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: 2 October 1995. And this is the site of Hodzici 2. The next exhibit, 167/4, showed the area where the site 3 will be created. This photograph is dated 7 September 1995. It just shows the dirt road and the hills around it with trees. And the second -- the Exhibit 167/5 shows the same terrain 2nd October 1995, where there is a clear disturbance of soil that marks the position of the Hodzici 3 site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So between the 7th of September, 1995, and the 2nd of October, 1995, the Hodzici Road 3 site -- secondary grave site was created?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: That is correct. Exhibit 167/6 shows a cluster of destroyed houses. The photograph is dated 7 September 1995. And in the vicinity of this cluster of destroyed houses, two sites will be created between the 7 September 1995 and the 7 October 1995. The Exhibit 167/7 shows that same terrain at the date of 2nd October, where --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me correct the record. The two sites were created, according to your testimony just a moment ago, between the 7th of September and the 7th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Sorry, a misspelling for me. It is the 2nd, not the 7th. It's my spelling that makes the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They were created between the 7th of September, 1995, and the 2nd of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The next exhibit, 167/8, is a photograph again dated 7 September 1995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, I'm sorry. Could you go back to the previous exhibit, the one on the 2nd of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, where now one can see two areas of disturbed soil that are, for us, the site of Hodzici 4 and Hodzici 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And have both of those sites been probed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, and they both contain remains. There has been exhumation also conducted there, full exhumation. I represent the Exhibit 167/8. It is another area along that so-called Hodzici road, also a cluster of destroyed houses. On that same terrain, the Exhibit 167/9, that is a photograph dated 7 October -- 2nd October 1995, where the site Hodzici 6 is clearly visible on that picture, a clear area of disturbed soil present there. That is also a confirmed secondary site. The Exhibit 167/10 shows the terrain in a location nearby the village of Cerik. That is still, for us, the Hodzici road. That photograph is dated 7 September 1995. There is nothing specific to see on this one. But on the Exhibit 167/11, that shows the same terrain at the date of 2nd October 1995, one can see that there is an area of disturbed soil. This is the site Hodzici 7, which is a confirmed secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So between the 7th of September, 1995, and the 2nd of October, 1995, HZ-7 was created?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you just keep that picture on the ELMO for a minute, Mr. Ruez. These are aerial images taken from a particular elevation above. Have you been to this particular series of secondary grave sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, I've been to this series of graves. But I didn't -- I was not part of the mission that we conducted to pinpoint them. I went to them after that, that is, another case for the other one we are talking about where -- was on the mission where we actually found them. These ones were found during another mission. We found these ones with the assistance of the aerial imagery. Without this aerial imagery provided by the US government, never ever would we have found this site south of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Because, as you will see on a film that we show later, vegetation grows very fast, and with the normal means of observation and probing, we would never have been able to find these places. The methods we used -- we used in 1996 to find graves and probe graves was not fairly sophisticated enough to enable us or give us a chance to find these sites with normal techniques. Without the assistance of imagery analysts, we would never have found these places south of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, have you finished now the testimony about the secondary sites along this particular road?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's turn now your attention to the third set of secondary mass graves, those at Liplje. Again, if you would kindly approach the large exhibit, using the pointer, and indicate where that cluster of secondary mass graves is located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The cluster of Liplje sites is just where the village of Liplje is marked on the map just south-west of Zvornik town. It is also a former Muslim village and is completed destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you give a general description of the terrain at that location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: All the area south-west of Zvornik is an area of hills and valleys. They just continue one after another. One could quickly get lost on all the paths which one can travel on with four-wheel drive vehicles in this area. There are a lot of hiding places there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I take it this is not a heavily populated area where this set of secondary graves was located.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Before 1992, it was populated. But during the war, I mean, just after the ethnic cleansing campaign of 1992, there were no Muslims left living in this area, and no one lived there during the last years. Now refugees, Muslim refugees, are returning in these areas and are trying to reconstruct their homes and their lives in this place. The problem is that all these secondary sites in their vicinity will have to be exhumed also before they can quietly resettle there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, please make your presentation in respect of these Liplje secondary mass graves sites.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The Exhibit 168/A is the map of the area of Zvornik that shows the precise location of the Liplje secondary graves, where we have four sites. The green dots numbered from 1 to 4 mark the locations of these graves. The next exhibit is 168/1, and it's an overview of the area of Liplje, where all the graves can be seen. From the right to the left, the right of the picture being the north on the ground, is Liplje 1 through Liplje 4. There is an additional problem now in this area. It's that the town of Zvornik is using the area in between the Liplje site 4 and the Liplje site 3, and has a garbage dump site for Zvornik town. The situation started in 1996, and now the garbage is at the edge of these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, LP-1 is the code for Liplje 1, and all the way through --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- to LP-4?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. "LP" is the code name for "Liplje."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Please proceed with your before-and-after images.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The next image will focus on the first site, which is Liplje 1. Exhibit 168/2 shows an area of completely destroyed houses where, aside from these destructions, nothing specific is to be observed. The photograph is dated 7 September 1995, so it is a "before" shot for the sites Liplje 1 and Liplje 2. Exhibit 168/3 is a photograph of the same location, with two differences on it -- really three differences. The first one is an area of disturbed soil behind a house, a destroyed house, and this is the location of grave Liplje 1; probed, confirmed presence of multiple remains in this site. On the same picture, one can see, more south, right, on the photograph, the location of the site of Liplje 2. That site had been fully exhumed. But one can also notice on that photograph that there is an area of disturbed soil at the top of the picture above Liplje 2 [indicates], which does not appear on the previous exhibit. Therefore, this is a location that we will still need to check. It might add one site in this area. Again, unfortunately, the investigation is far from being over on that topic, and the disclosure of all of these elements is going to put at risk all the people who will be doing the job there. The next exhibit is 168/4, and there is no "before" shot for this site. But one could assume that if we had a photograph dated 7 September 1995 to show you, we would see that there is nothing specific in that location. This one is dated 7 October 1995 and shows an area of disturbed soil. That is, for us, the site Liplje 3 which had been probed and confirmed as a secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, to clarify the record again, your testimony reflects a date of the 7th of October, 1995. I think you had meant the 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: 2nd October 1995. On this photograph, also the title says "Snagovo." Again, it's just a question of naming the place. We call all these sites Liplje, even though this is not exactly Liplje village. It's just that Liplje is the main village in this area. The next exhibit is 168/5. It is again a photograph dated 7 September 1995, where there is nothing specific to be observed aside from destroyed houses. For your information, the garbage dump site I was talking about has now invaded all the area south of this photograph and is now at the edge of this gravel road [indicates], not immediately threatening the secondary sites, but they are in a very close vicinity of the sites. The next exhibit is 168/6. It is a photograph dated 2nd October 1995, and shows that behind one of these destroyed houses is an area of disturbed soil, and this site has been checked and confirmed also as being a secondary mass grave containing multiple human remains. The following photograph is Exhibit 168/7. It is a colour photograph taken from a helicopter on 15 June 1996. It is designed to show you how the ground looks from the air, but in colour. I'm going to point on the picture the locations of two graves which are in the frame of this picture, which are Liplje 1 and Liplje 2. The other sites are out of the frame. The circle I've just marked here is the location of Liplje 1 and then can be compared with the aerial photograph to have a better reference on the ground; and the second site, that is Liplje 2 has been fully exhumed, and it's located where I'm going to circle now [marks], just here on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, would you put an "LP-1" and an "LP-2" so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: [Marks]. Done. The last photograph is Exhibit 168/1 [sic] and it shows the result of a quick probe that was conducted there when we first went to this area. That was in 1997. That is a very shallow grave with human remains inside. Many bones are scattered around. All these bones have attracted a lot of attention these last weeks in the area and things will have to be done this summer to solve this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just to clarify the record, the record reflects that this exhibit that's on the ELMO, in the record is 168/1 and it should be 168/8.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This concludes the presentation for the Liplje sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, let's go to our final location and final cluster of secondary mass grave sites on the Cancari road. Using the pointer, please indicate on the large map the location of the Cancari road.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The Cancari road is located south of Zvornik again. It is a valley which is quite long. It's a 10-kilometre-long valley entering this area, and there is a possibility to exit this valley also, to hit another road that then goes through Sekovici to Tisce, or then going north one can go towards Zvornik. This is a difficult area to access which is possible with normal vehicles. It would not be the choice of a truck driver. The entrance of the valley is just at the Drina, where the Drina River is, and it is a main road that goes from Vlasenica to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you describe the terrain, please.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: It's a long and narrow valley at some point but larger at other ones. It's an area completely destroyed also. Again, it's an area which was in the majority populated by Muslims, but not only probably. Combat also has taken place in all this area in 1993 and 1994, so the destruction here is a mixture of dynamiting houses and combat activities. This is the main cluster of graves that we have. There are 12 secondary graves along a stretch of eight kilometres of dirt road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, continue with your presentation about the secondary graves at Cancari road.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 169/A is a map of the area that spots the precise location of all these graves, starting from the east to the west with number 1 through number 12. I show on the map the location of the site number 1, and you can see that then the road heads north. This one will not appear on the next exhibit which is an overview of all the sites, with the exception of number 1 which will be out of the frame of the aerial imagery. The next exhibit is a photograph of that same road, so a mosaic of several pictures to reconstruct the road. I will have to flip it through the ELMO, starting from west towards the east, in reverse order. So Cancari 12, and continuing along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The site number 1 will be just at the bottom corner of the last photograph on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So the record is clear, "CR" is the code designation for Cancari road.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the numbers designate the specific secondary mass grave sites.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, our next exhibit is going to be a film. It will be approximately ten minutes. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 169/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, would you explain to the Judges what they will be seeing on this particular film, and the purpose for showing it.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. In reality there is not much to be seen on that film, and this is the purpose of showing it. The film was filmed while we were conducting the exhumation -- I mean, Professor Richard Wright was conducting the exhumation at the Cancari 12 site. We used the opportunity of his presence to pinpoint for him the location of all the other sites. So I used the opportunity to take very brief video footage of all these sites, with the exception of 12 where the exhumation was ongoing, in order to show how the terrain looks like after a couple of years of vegetation growing in these places. So in reality there will be nothing to be seen on the film aside from vegetation, but this is the interest of the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The vegetation shows that -- conceals, in fact, the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Shows that it is very well-concealed, and if someone has not very, very precise information -- in fact, from an aerial photograph there is nearly no way that you would find the place except if he knows where he dug the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could dim the lights, please, and if we could show Prosecutor's Exhibit 169/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, please feel free to make comments during the transmission of this film.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So this site is the site of Cancari 11. The site, in fact, was just at the right when I started to film, and here I'm doing kind of a 360-degree tour. Just at the left here is a Muslim cemetery. The film is dated summer 1998. So the location of the grave is just there, right in the middle of the picture. No one would notice any difference in the soil if he would not know that there is a grave here. And here I'm zooming on a few other gravestones. So here the site has been obviously created on purpose in a former cemetery. No steady shot of the camera, I'm sorry. This is why the picture is moving so much. This is now the Cancari 10 site which is here, just in front. No difference with the rest. And here you can see the shape of the houses in this environment. Now the site number 9. Site number 9 is now here where these -- just here, where these white stones are, just alongside the road. Now Cancari 8. Cancari 8 is just here where these bushes are visible. The only thing visible are bushes. Cancari 7 is just in front of a destroyed house. Woodcutters were operating there and strangely never dumped any wood there, on the site, but always just next to it. That could give the feeling that they knew what was there. Just here. A very, very shallow grave; less than 10 centimetres of soil on top of the bodies, before reaching the bodies, the body parts. That's another view of the same site. Just in between this destroyed vehicle and the house in the background is the site. Now site number 6 which is just where the film starts. Here, as you can see, the valley is larger than in the other locations. It's a very deserted area; no one was living there during the years. Also, there are a certain number of mine signs in this area, either for real mines or for deterrence of people to wander in the area. The signs I'm talking about are generally pots that are hanging on branches and that indicates to locals that there are potential mines around the houses. Site number 5 is just here where this group of bushes are, just alongside the road, just where these bushes are growing on top of it. One indication of the presence of a grave is sometimes the vegetation grows faster than on other spots, but it's not enough for someone to be able to be sure that there is something there. Number 4, that is very nearby number 5 and has been fully exhumed. It's just here. So here you have some indication still because -- there are some spots where there is no vegetation, but even that would not be enough to indicate the presence of a grave. Someone would not know precisely where to find it. This is the site. This is now the Cancari 3 site. Sorry. It's this one that has been fully exhumed, Cancari 3. And here is the site, just where the camera showed it now. So just on the opposite side of this dirt road is the site. Now it's Cancari 2, but it's even more concealed because it's even a little side path that cuts the main path, so this one is even more concealed. And the site is in front of this house, on the other side where the logs are, on the left of the picture. I don't film it straight but at that time I thought it was another place. Here you have an example of a pot hanging on a branch. That would deter any local to approach this place. It might be a genuine mine threat. There are many of these pots in the area; I just filmed a few as an example. That's a way to indicate the presence of mines. Putting stones like a pyramid is also a way to indicate mines. This is not a site. This is a mosque. It was a mosque. That was the minaret before it was apparently fully destroyed. That is to indicate that, indeed, it was a Muslim-populated area. There is no randomness also in the choice of these locations. The fact that they are all Muslim villages is certainly not a random fact. The last, the first or the last, is Cancari 1, just in front here, in the fork of the main path and the subpath.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, now would you take us through the before-and-after images --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- of Cancari 1 through Cancari 12.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: The first site, Cancari 1, it will -- for all these series of photographs, they will all be framed between 7 September 1995 and 7 [sic] October 1995. So the first one, the Cancari 1 site --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me again correct the record. They will be framed between 7 September 1995 and, the record says, "7 October 1995." Do you mean 2 October?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, 2 October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: So the photograph dated 7 September 1995, where the site Cancari 1 will be created later, so Exhibit 169/4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the previous exhibit is 169/3 that's on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- the "before" picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Correct. It shows the same area but with a date of October 2nd, and it shows clearly the area of the disturbance. This site was probed. All of them have been probed. Some of them have even been probed twice; once when we found them and another later on by Professor Wright to ensure that the assessment is 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "probed," the conclusions of the probing was that there were multiple human remains found at each of these locations.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: I could have also shown you photographs of these remains for each of these sites, but it would have been much more lengthy, and you will see more of these things later on anyhow so it would have been a bit useless. Exhibit 169/5 is a photograph dated 7 September 1995 showing where the Cancari 2 site will be created, and the photograph dated October 2nd shows where the site, indeed, is, just in front of a destroyed house, so quite a way from the main road. Here the concealment effort has been even pushed further. Exhibit 169/7 is a photograph dated 7 September showing the location where the Cancari 3 site will be created, and Exhibit 169/8 shows the location of this site. It is marked on the picture "CR-3," where the disturbed soil is visible. Exhibit 169/9, a photograph dated 7 September 1995, and this is the area where, at 2nd October 1995, there will be present two sites: Cancari 4 and Cancari 5. This is the Exhibit 169/10, a photograph dated October 2nd, with two areas of clear disturbed soil; probed and confirmed secondary mass grave sites. Exhibit 169/11, a photograph dated 7 September. Again, on the titles, the names change. This one is Redzici. The reason is that the closest village is Redzici. We call all this valley Cancari. The next photograph shows the location of the CR-6 site in this area, and that will be Exhibit 169/12, a photograph dated 2 October, showing the spot where the Cancari 6 grave has been created between 7 September and 7 October -- 2 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ruez, let me just stop you on that image right there. Are there traces of heavy engineering equipment being used at this location in this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. All these traces of disturbance are not done by manual digging but by heavy equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Exhibit 169/13 is a photograph dated 7 September and shows the site number 7 just in between a destroyed house and the road, nearby a destroyed vehicle. And 2 October 1995 is the Exhibit 169/14. The site is marked on the photograph and the vehicle that you could see on the film dated 1998 was already there in 1995. I'm going to circle it on the picture [marks]. This gives you another reference of objects viewed from the air. Exhibit 169/15 is a photograph dated October 2nd. There is no "before" shot for this one, not in my possession at this moment anyhow. It shows where the Cancari 8 site has been created. A photograph dated 7 September certainly exists -- I don't have it in my possession -- but it would show that there was nothing there at that time. It was created between 7 September and 2 October. Exhibit 169/16 is a photograph dated 7 September 1995. The area where something will appear is where I will put a circle [marks], more or less in the centre of this picture dated 7 September. We have another one dated 27 September 1995. That is the Exhibit 169/17. That shows that in between 7 September and 27 September 1995 an open pit was created on that spot. You can clearly see the open trench here which is not filled yet. Exhibit 169/18 will show that between 27 September 1995 and 2 October 1995 the grave was filled, and this is Exhibit 169/18, where now you can see the disturbed soil. That is, in fact, an indication that the trench has been filled with one, two, or three truckloads of human remains and then closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's site CR-9.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This is the site CR-9. The next exhibit is 169/19. It will show where the CR-10 site has been created. It will be just in front of the destroyed house, on the opposite side of the path. I will circle it [marks]. This will be the location. Exhibit 169/20 is a photograph dated 27 September 1995 and shows that, indeed, between 7 September and 27 September, an open trench has been created on that spot. Exhibit 169/21 is a photograph dated 2 October 1995. It clearly shows that between 27 September and 2 October the site has been filled with human remains. This is CR-10 site. Exhibit 169/22 is dated 7 September 1995. There is on this one still nothing to be seen. I'm marking with a circle the area where something will be visible [marks]. The 27 September 1995, this will be the Exhibit 169/23, is a photograph dated 27 September 1995 showing that in between the 7th and the 27th, again an open trench has been created here. It is clearly visible on the photograph [marks]. I'm circling this open trench [marks]. The Exhibit 169/24 shows that between 27 September and the 2nd of October, this open pit has been used and filled with what we know are multiple human remains. This is the site CR-11. Exhibit 169/25 is a photograph dated 7 September, and it shows the terrain where later on also a trench will be opened in the area I have just circled [marks]. The next photograph is Exhibit 169/26, dated 27 September 1995, and shows the creation of a trench [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again on that particular image, Mr. Ruez, are there traces of heavy construction equipment evident?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes. You can see large tyre tracks which most probably had been made by an excavator on wheels, UNT-type, UNT machine. The following exhibit is 169/27 and is a photograph dated 7 -- 2nd October 1995, showing that the trench that existed the 27th has been filled between the 27th September and the 2nd of October. This site has been fully exhumed in 1998 and contained -- I don't have a precise number in my head, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You don't have to worry about that, Mr. Ruez. There will be subsequent testimony about the number of bodies that were exhumed from that particular site.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn, Mr. Ruez, because our next exhibit is going to be a film, Prosecutor's Exhibit 169/28 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, perhaps we need to have a break, because to continue until 2.30 without a break, I think, it will be too much for the interpreters. So maybe we should have a 15-minute break now, and then we'll go on until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we're now going to see a film, Prosecutor's Exhibit 169/28. And as we usually do, will you please inform the Judges and the public gallery what will be seen on this particular piece of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: This film will show the exhumation in Cancari 12 site. It was the first full exhumation of a secondary site, so it will be only an example of that kind of activity that we will present to you visually in film format.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could reduce the lights, please, and if we could play Prosecutor's Exhibit 169/28, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, please feel free to comment during the course of this viewing. I think we have a re-run. Is this a film we have previously seen or is this --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ
utterances.text: No, this should be the good one. We initially saw the location of the site, and this is the surroundings. This is a film that I had filmed at the time of the exhumation. This is the path leading towards Cancari 11 and the exit of a valley. This is a 360-degree tour of the environment of this site. There is a mixed resettling there. Some Serbs were settling in the area in 1998, and now Muslims are returning in the area. These are two surveyors who are, in fact, creating a very precise map of the grave area, and you will see them later on plotting every single object inside the grave. This is Richard Wright seen from the back, and the little backhoe is now scooping the soil in order to identify the perimeter of the grave. That's the first activity that Professor Wright does on a grave site. So the first part of the process is to scoop the surface. At one point, we'll see that there is a difference of colour in the soil. And here Richard Wright just marked this, and now he's putting flags on this perimeter. Here you can see on the left and the right there is already a difference. This is now making the tour of the grave. This is already the end of one side of the grave. Due to the way the digging machine initially created that grave, in fact, there were remains beyond the initial separation line of the two types of soils. This gives you already here the beginning of the shape of the grave. The excavator is used only during the hardest work, but after that, everything turns manual. The blank is normally -- no, it's not finished yet. It's a normal blank, because we changed days. So here they are doing the tour of the grave, and all the mound in the middle is already the content of the grave. They are currently narrowing down the size of it, and here the first human remains start to appear. Since it is a secondary site, there are very few complete bodies in it, due to the way the initial burial was conducted using heavy equipment, then the unburial using again heavy equipment, then the transportation in trucks, the dumping from the trucks, the refilling of the hole with heavy equipment. All this destroys the bodies under. You end up only with a mixture of body parts. This was a -- this is a hand popping out of a mound of soil, which is now being protected with plastic. These are skulls popping out of the soil. Here is a shoe. Here you can see a colleague using a metal detector in order to find shell casings mixed with the bodies. As we said, we had collected an amount of shell casings on every execution site, and now here the aim is to collect also shell casings. The aim is then, later on, to compare these shell casings and make connections between execution site, primary mass grave, and later on secondary mass grave. Here the members of the exhumation team are on top of the grave, and they are cleaning the surface of it. This is the first shell casing found. Due to the style of the executions, the shell casings were mixed with the bodies, so then when the bodies were taken away, the shell casings were taken away as well. Professor Wright will be able to provide you with detailed explanations regarding his methodology, but you can already observe that this is real archaeological work. The aim is not to pull the bodies outside of the soil but to make sure that nothing is missed and every part is properly preserved. This is how the grave looks like once the surface of it has already been cleaned. This site probably contained -- I mean the measurement unit for this site is truckload, so this would probably be two truckloads or three truckloads. Professor Wright might have more details on this. Every evening the site is covered, filmed, refilmed the next morning to ensure that nothing happened during the night, and it is guarded during the night. It's not finished. This is again the hand that was protected with the plastic bag. That day they continued the work around it. The little noise means a positive reaction to metal. This is the grave filmed from above. There are often changes in the concentration of all these body parts probably linked with dumping from the truck which transported all these remains from the primary site to this secondary one. Just for an indication, these bodies are coming from the Branjevo Farm. Once this phase was completed, the process of retrieving the body parts started. These are the surveyors plotting every object before it is retrieved from the grave, every object and also every body part. The element missing on the film, for sure, is the smell. This is an example of the difficulties these experts encounter when they have to retrieve body parts in such a mixture of bodies. I made this piece short but it lasted probably an hour, to retrieve just this one part; the problem being to follow the part to make sure that it won't get disconnected with what is attached to it in the process of retrieving the body. It was a leg. It took them a long time to retrieve this part. This is three years after the events and one can see that some of the parts are still well-preserved. I don't think that was supposed to be the end but -- it was not the end. Could we be informed about the reason why it's finished.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I spoke with the technical booth and they said that was all that was on the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can raise the lights. We've finished with the exhibit. Mr. Ruez, I have concluded my examination. Mr. President, Judge Wald, that concludes the presentation of Mr. Ruez on direct examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we will resume perhaps tomorrow with the cross-examination of Mr. Ruez. For today we cannot continue. We will meet again tomorrow, here, at 9.30.
